page: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the arm64 architecture. Powered by Microsoft custom ARM processors utilizing the Neoverse-N2 core design at 3.4 GHz, it provides 32 dedicated physical cores across 32 vCPUs with one thread per core. The instance is equipped with 256 GB of memory, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, backed by 128 MB of L3 cache. It also includes 1888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without integrated graphics acceleration.

Benchmark measurements highlight high memory subsystem performance and strong multi-core scalability. The instance scores in the top tier for uncached large block memory bandwidth, achieving 449.0 GB/sec for reads and 188.31 GB/sec for writes. PassMark database operations and PassMark overall memory benchmarks similarly land in the top tier. In CPU-bound multi-threaded execution, stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core place in the top 25 percent, while single-core metrics across stress-ng and Geekbench remain in the middle tier.

Hardware tradeoffs center around the ARM Neoverse-N2 execution characteristics. While the platform offers substantial memory bandwidth and competitive throughput per watt, single-threaded operations perform in the average range. Furthermore, the absence of discrete GPUs limits large language model inference; large 70B parameter models demonstrate low token processing rates, whereas smaller models execute adequately on CPU.

Given the fast local NVMe storage and high memory allocation, the E32pds_v6 is suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching layers, compilation tasks, and multi-threaded data analytics that require significant memory density and sustained memory throughput.
description: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v6 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated ARM Neoverse-N2 cores operating at 3.4 GHz on the arm64 architecture. It provides 256 GB of system RAM, yielding 8 GB per vCPU, along with 128 MB of L3 cache and a bundled 1888 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating without hardware GPU acceleration, the server demonstrates exceptional memory bandwidth, reaching 449.0 GB/sec in uncached read benchmarks and placing in the top tier for PassMark database operations. Multi-core performance is robust across stress-ng and Geekbench testing, contrasting with average single-thread ratings. The balance of high memory density, substantial bandwidth, and integrated high-speed local disk storage aligns with memory-heavy workloads, including in-memory data grids, large database servers, enterprise software compilation, and scalable web backend infrastructure.
